subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: After live current-main Copilot Claude isolated-cron proof, should aborted or no-output Copilot runs enter model fallback, or should OpenClaw rely on shorter idle-timeout failure plus cron error status?
rationale: Source shows partial mitigation but the remaining fallback policy can recover delivery or repeat side effects, and the closed-unmerged fallback-seeding PR does not settle the product boundary.

options.title: Prove first, fallback narrowly
options.body: Run live Copilot cron proof and allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

options.title: Fallback on no-output aborts
options.body: Classify aborted/no-output Copilot runs as fallback-worthy whenever a configured fallback exists, accepting the retry-policy risk.

options.title: Do not expand fallback
options.body: Keep current cron error surfacing and shorter idle-timeout behavior without adding a new aborted-result retry path.

recommendation.title: Prove first, fallback narrowly
recommendation.body: Run live Copilot cron proof and allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate for the Copilot provider stream and embedded-runner timeout policy surfaces identified in the existing review history.
